source.title: A Multi-fidelity Double-Delta Wing Dataset and Empirical Scaling Laws for GNN-based Aerodynamic Field Surrogate

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures data-size scaling in a non-language GNN surrogate and qualifies the observed power law: it identifies a limited power-law region and reports departures associated with small data and a fixed compute budget.
record.gate_note: The study tests scaling for an aerodynamic field-prediction GNN using held-out test MSE, not language-model pretraining loss. It cites language-model scaling work, but cited results are not recorded as rows. The per-dataset-size MSE values appear only in figures; the text describes their trends but does not give the individual values.
record.test_reason: The study tests data-size power laws in a new setting: supervised aerodynamic field prediction with a GNN. Its own held-out MSE results bear on V5 and on V7's curve-bending and setup-dependence components. It does not test language-model scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors report preliminary power-law data scaling with a collective exponent of −0.6122 and estimate sampling requirements under their training budget. They conjecture that larger models use data more efficiently and that insufficient compute explains the Large-model anomaly. They explicitly call for joint compute, model and data scaling to obtain more robust conclusions; the causal compute explanations are not experimentally verified.
record.recipe_differences: This is an empirical data-scaling study for an aerodynamic GNN surrogate, using held-out MSE and fixed-budget data-size sweeps; it is not the language-model pretraining-loss or compute-optimal-allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior differs by data-size region and model size. The authors identify D ≤ 80 as small-data, 80 ≤ D ≤ 320 as power-law, and D ≥ 320 as compute-limited asymptotic error; the Large model departs from the exponent-versus-size trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Inverting the fitted curves against assumed target losses yields dataset sizes of 261, 245, 317 and 261 graphs and an estimated sampling density of eight points per dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A fitted surrogate learning curve can estimate geometric sampling requirements conditional on an assumed target loss and training budget.

record.problems: The authors call the scaling analysis preliminary. The holdout test set has 80 graphs from 16 geometries; each setting is repeated six times. Compute is fixed rather than systematically varied, the largest model's trend is anomalous, and per-size MSE values are shown in figures rather than stated numerically.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and its parameter, token, or compute scaling over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of independently evaluated runs orders of magnitude larger than the fitting runs. Inverting a fitted curve for target dataset sizes does not test this.
Loss-minimising parameter/data allocation and stable allocation exponents across compute budgets.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count; width and attention heads change together with parameter count.
Modalities and training regimes beyond this supervised, physics-informed aerodynamic GNN; broad-range power-law validity beyond the factor-four fitting interval.
Downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss; the measured MSE is the surrogate's direct prediction loss.

Controlled sensitivity to fitting method, parameter counting, schedules or data definitions; compute-optimal splits and disagreement between published language-model laws. Increasing compute to test the proposed cause of saturation and the Large-model anomaly is left to future work.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used; figure curves cannot be independently read. Point-row states describe the presence of V5's power-law behavior; departures themselves support V7. The fitting boundaries overlap the named neighboring regimes, so D = 80 and D = 320 should not be classified as failed power-law points. The budget fixes a maximum of 2000 updates per fold, four folds, with early stopping; equal update limits across model sizes do not establish equal FLOPs. No challenges label is warranted for saturation under an acknowledged training bottleneck.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
No validation that laws fitted on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study does not find a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation across compute budgets.
It varies model size but does not test depth, width, or architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
Tests data-size scaling for an aerodynamic GNN surrogate; does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream-task performance scaling is measured.

Does not compare parameter-counting conventions, fitting methods, or data/training schedules systematically, and does not test compute-optimal splits or disagreement between the cited language-model laws.
